---
title: "Single-cell: comparing conditions"
description: >
  Does a condition change which cells are present, or where they sit on the
  embedding? summarize_group_meta(), get_meta_pivot(),
  plot_composition_scatter(), plot_composition_bars() and
  DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit().
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_common.R")
```

**Question:** between two conditions, do the proportions of cell types change,
and where on the embedding are cells gained or lost?

| Function | Use |
|---|---|
| `summarize_group_meta()` | counts and proportions per group, condition (and sample) |
| `get_meta_pivot()` | a quick two-way table of two metadata columns |
| `plot_composition_scatter()` | proportion of each group in one condition against another |
| `plot_composition_bars()` | stacked bars of the composition of each condition or sample, from any table |
| `DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit()` | where on an embedding a condition has more or fewer cells |

These plots describe differences; they do not test them. Cells from one
sample are not independent replicates, so tests of composition must use
samples (e.g. propeller, scCODA, Milo).

**Data:** 8,000 PBMCs from [Kang et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042),
8 donors, each sampled as control and after 6 h of interferon-β (IFN-β): 16
samples.

```{r data}
pbmc <- docs_kang()
```

## Counting cells

`summarize_group_meta()` counts the cells of each group per condition (and
per sample with `sample.by`) and their proportion of the condition's cells.
It takes a Seurat object or its metadata.

```{r summarize}
comp <- summarize_group_meta(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", split.by = "condition")
head(comp)
```

```{r summarize-samples}
per_sample <- summarize_group_meta(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    sample.by = "donor"
)
head(per_sample, 3)
```

`get_meta_pivot()` gives a two-way table of any two columns, as counts or as
percentages of rows, columns or the total:

```{r pivot}
get_meta_pivot(pbmc$cell_type, pbmc$condition, type = "count")
get_meta_pivot(
    pbmc$cell_type,
    pbmc$condition,
    type = "percent",
    margin = "column"
)
```

## Composition scatter

Each group's proportion in one condition (x) against the other (y), with the
y = x line: groups above it are more abundant in the y condition.

```{r composition}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    x = "Control",
    y = "IFN-beta"
)
```

Six hours of IFN-β leave the cell type composition almost unchanged: all
cell types lie on the line. The response is a change of state, seen in the
expression of interferon-stimulated genes (see
[Expression across groups](sc-expression.html)).

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `sample.by`

Proportions per sample, each point the mean of a condition's samples, so that
every donor counts the same. The horizontal bar is computed from the samples
of the x condition and the vertical bar from those of the y condition:
`error` chooses the SEM (default), the SD of the samples, or a 95% confidence
interval of the mean (`"ci95"`, mean ± t(0.975, n - 1) × SEM, t-based since
there are few samples per condition).

```{r comp-samples}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    sample.by = "donor"
)
```

```{r comp-ci}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    sample.by = "donor",
    error = "ci95",
    log = TRUE
)
```

#### `log` and `fold.lines`

Log axes spread rare groups; `fold.lines = 2` draws y = 2x and y = x / 2:

```{r comp-log}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    log = TRUE,
    fold.lines = 2
)
```

#### `value = "count"`

Numbers of cells instead of proportions:

```{r comp-count}
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    value = "count",
    log = TRUE
)
```

#### `facet.by`

One panel per level of a third column, with proportions computed within
each, e.g. within lymphoid and myeloid cells:

```{r comp-facet}
is_lymphoid <- pbmc$cell_type %in% c("CD4 T", "CD8 T", "NK", "B")
pbmc$lineage <- factor(
    ifelse(is_lymphoid, "Lymphoid", "Myeloid"),
    levels = c("Lymphoid", "Myeloid")
)
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    facet.by = "lineage",
    panel.width = 2.2,
    cells = colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$cell_type != "Megakaryocyte"]
)
```

## Composition bars

Stacked bars: one bar per level of `split.by`, one coloured segment per level
of `group.by`, and one panel per level of `facet.by`. The segments of a bar
are shares of that bar's cells, so every bar adds up to 100%. One bar per
donor, in a panel per condition, shows how much samples vary:

```{r bars}
plot_composition_bars(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    facet.by = "condition"
)
```

Swapping `group.by` and `split.by` answers another question: which samples
make up each cell type (e.g. whether a cluster comes from one sample only).

Bars have a fixed width (`bar.width`), gap (`bar.gap`) and length
(`bar.length`) in inches, and panels a fixed gap (`panel.spacing`), so the
figure keeps its proportions whatever the number of bars. Bars and segments
have black borders (`border.width`, in points), and the value axis shows its
ticks and labels without a line (`value.axis.line = TRUE` draws it).

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `connect`

Bands joining each group's segments in neighbouring bars of a panel, in a
light tone of its colour: `"curve"` (as in alluvial plots) or `"straight"`.
Off by default (`"none"`). `connect.lighten` sets how light the bands are,
as the share of white mixed into the colour (default 0.8; 0 is the group's
own colour).

```{r bars-connect}
plot_composition_bars(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    facet.by = "condition",
    connect = "curve"
)
```

```{r bars-straight}
plot_composition_bars(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    connect = "straight",
    bar.width = 0.5,
    bar.gap = 0.5
)
```

#### `flip` and `label`

Horizontal bars, first bar on top. `label = TRUE` writes each segment's
share inside it (white on dark segments), for segments of at least
`label.min` (5%) whose text fits:

```{r bars-flip}
plot_composition_bars(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    flip = TRUE,
    label = TRUE,
    bar.width = 0.4
)
```

#### `value` and `show.n`

`"fraction"` (0 to 1) or `"count"` (numbers of cells, bars of different
lengths) instead of percentages; `show.n = TRUE` writes each bar's number of
cells beyond its end:

```{r bars-fraction}
plot_composition_bars(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    value = "fraction"
)
```

```{r bars-count}
plot_composition_bars(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    facet.by = "condition",
    value = "count",
    show.n = TRUE
)
```

#### `order.by`

Bars of each panel sorted by decreasing share of one group:

```{r bars-order}
plot_composition_bars(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    facet.by = "condition",
    order.by = "CD14 Mono"
)
```

#### Legend

`legend.title`, `legend.position` and `legend.ncol`, as in
`DimPlot_bioToolkit()`:

```{r bars-legend}
plot_composition_bars(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    facet.by = "condition",
    legend.title = "Cell type",
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.ncol = 4
)
```

#### Any table

The rows need not be cells: any table with categorical columns works (a
gene or peak annotation, DE results), and `unit` names what a row is. Here,
the direction of each gene in the pseudobulk DE of IFN-β against control,
per cell type:

```{r bars-genes}
de <- docs_kang_de()
direction_of <- function(res) {
    sig <- res$FDR < 0.05
    out <- ifelse(res$logFC > 0, "Up", "Down")
    out[!sig] <- "Not significant"
    factor(out, levels = c("Up", "Down", "Not significant"))
}
de_genes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(de), function(ct) {
    data.frame(
        cell_type = factor(ct, levels = names(de)),
        direction = direction_of(de[[ct]])
    )
}))
direction_cols <- c(
    "Up" = "#D62728",
    "Down" = "#1F77B4",
    "Not significant" = "#D9D9D9"
)
plot_composition_bars(
    de_genes,
    group.by = "direction",
    split.by = "cell_type",
    unit = "genes",
    cols = direction_cols,
    show.n = TRUE
)
```

## Density difference on the embedding

`DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit()` estimates the density of cells of each
condition on the embedding (normalized, so cell numbers do not matter) and
draws the difference from a reference condition: magenta where the compared
condition has relatively more cells, blue where it has fewer. The colour
scale is centred on 0 and each side reaches its full colour at its own
extreme. With `sample.by`, each sample's density is computed separately and
averaged, so one large sample cannot drive the map.

What the map means depends on the embedding. On the **integrated** UMAP
(Harmony over condition), cells of both conditions are aligned by cell type,
so the map shows shifts within cell types:

```{r density}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    label = TRUE,
    label.by = "cell_type"
)
```

On the UMAP **before integration**, IFN-β-stimulated cells of every type sit
apart from their controls, and the map shows that response as a separation:

```{r density-raw}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    reduction = "umap.unintegrated",
    label = TRUE,
    label.by = "cell_type"
)
```

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `measure = "log2ratio"`

The log2 ratio of the two densities instead of their difference: fold
changes, which also show sparse regions.

```{r density-ratio}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    measure = "log2ratio"
)
```

#### `draw = "raster"` and `contour`

The density difference drawn as a continuous surface, with contours of the
density of all cells:

```{r density-raster}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    draw = "raster",
    contour = TRUE
)
```

#### `density.adjust`

The bandwidth multiplier: below 1 resolves smaller regions, above 1 smooths
more.

```{r density-adjust}
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    density.adjust = 0.5
)
```
